subject: maths
title: Column Addition and Subtraction
seo_title: Year 4 Column Addition and Subtraction Worksheets: Exchanging, Checking and Two-Step Problems
standard_text: Add and subtract numbers with up to 4 digits using the formal written methods of columnar addition and subtraction where appropriate; estimate and use inverse operations to check answers to a calculation; solve addition and subtraction two-step problems in contexts, deciding which operations and methods to use and why.
meta_desc: Free Year 4 maths worksheets on column addition and subtraction with 4-digit numbers, following the National Curriculum: exchanging, subtracting across zeros, estimating, checking with the inverse and two-step word problems. 100 questions with an answer key.
key_big: Line up the ones. Start on the right. Exchange when you need to.
key_sub: Adding: a column of 10 or more exchanges 1 into the next column. Subtracting: if the top digit is smaller, exchange 1 from the next column, and every 0 you pass becomes 9. Check with the inverse or an estimate.
body_html:
The idea: line up the columns

Write the numbers in columns so ones are under ones, tens under tens, hundreds under hundreds and thousands under thousands. Always start with the ones on the right.

When a column adds up to 10 or more, write the ones digit and exchange 10 for 1 in the next column on the left. Write the exchanged 1 small, under the answer line.

Column subtraction with exchanging

Always take the bottom digit from the top digit. If the top digit is smaller, exchange: take 1 from the next column on the left and make 10 more in this column. Cross out the old digit and write the new one above it.

Exchanging across zeros

If the next column is 0, there is nothing to take. Move left to the first digit that is not 0 and exchange from there, one column at a time. Every 0 you pass becomes 9.

Different numbers of digits

What is 4,567 + 382?

Write 382 under the 567 so the ones line up: 2 under 7, 8 under 6, 3 under 5. Ones: 7 + 2 = 9. Tens: 6 + 8 = 14, write 4 and exchange. Hundreds: 5 + 3 + 1 = 9. Thousands: 4.

Answer: 4,949

Check your answer

Use the inverse. Addition and subtraction undo each other. To check 5,213 − 2,768 = 2,445, add: 2,445 + 2,768 = 5,213. You get back to the start, so the answer is right.

Estimate. Round each number to the nearest hundred and do the easier calculation. 5,213 − 2,768 is about 5,200 − 2,800 = 2,400. An answer of 2,445 is sensible. An answer of 3,555 is not.

Two-step problems

Read the question and ask: what do I need to find first? Decide whether each step is adding (putting together, more) or subtracting (taking away, how many left, how many more). Then check the answer makes sense.

Two steps

A theatre has 9,500 tickets. It sold 3,486 on Friday and 4,275 on Saturday. How many tickets are left?

Step 1, tickets sold: 3,486 + 4,275 = 7,761. Step 2, tickets left: 9,500 − 7,761 = 1,739. Check: 1,739 + 7,761 = 9,500.

Answer: 1,739 tickets

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Forgetting the exchanged 1 (4,567 + 3,856 = 7,313)Write the exchanged 1 under the next column and add it in
Taking the smaller digit from the bigger one (5,213 − 2,768 = 3,555)Always take the bottom digit from the top digit. Exchange when the top is smaller
Not exchanging across a zero (4,002 − 1,358 = 2,354)Go left to the first digit that is not 0. Each 0 you pass becomes 9
Lining up the numbers on the left (4,567 + 382 = 8,387)Line up the ones on the right

faq.q: What is column addition and subtraction in Year 4?
faq.a: It is the formal written method: write the numbers in columns by place value and work from the ones to the left, exchanging when needed. In Year 4 pupils use it with numbers up to 4 digits.

faq.q: What does “exchange” mean in column subtraction?
faq.a: Exchanging means swapping 1 from the next column for 10 in this column, for example 1 ten for 10 ones. It is what older books call borrowing or carrying.

faq.q: How do you subtract from a number with zeros, like 4,002 − 1,358?
faq.a: Go left to the first digit that is not 0 and exchange from there. 4,002 becomes 3 thousands, 9 hundreds, 9 tens and 12 ones, and the answer is 2,644.

faq.q: How can my child check an addition or subtraction answer?
faq.a: Use the inverse: for 5,213 − 2,768 = 2,445, check that 2,445 + 2,768 = 5,213. A quick estimate, such as 5,200 − 2,800 = 2,400, also shows whether the answer is sensible.

sets.title: Estimate and check with the inverse

items.q: Which calculation checks 5,213 − 2,768 = 2,445?
items.e: Addition is the inverse of subtraction. Add the answer to the number you took away: 2,445 + 2,768 = 5,213. That is the number you started with, so the answer is right.
